cards.text: Israel's dividing up the land of Canaan, and now we get the allotment for the clans of the tribe of Judah. The south runs from the Salt Sea past Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Egypt, the east is the Salt Sea, the north climbs right past the Jebusites at Jerusalem, and the west is the Great Sea. That border takes more turns than I did feeling my way around the back of a junk drawer in the dark.
Then Joshua gives Caleb son of Jephunneh a portion among the sons of Judah, and this is no 'my cousin knows a guy' deal. Joshua does it according to the LORD's command.

cards.question: Which city does Joshua give to Caleb?

cards.text: Hebron's other name is Kiriath-arba, and Arba was the forefather of Anak. So Caleb gets a city with the other family's name still on the MAILBOX.

cards.question: Caleb's new city of Hebron has descendants of Anak in it. What does Caleb do about them?

cards.text: Caleb just drove out three sons of Anak, and does he take a nap? NO. He marches against Debir, once called Kiriath-sepher, and makes an offer to whoever captures it.

cards.question: Caleb says the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it will get his ___ in marriage.
True or false: The man who captures Kiriath-sepher is Caleb's own nephew.

cards.text: So Othniel, son of Caleb's brother Kenaz, takes the city and marries Caleb's daughter Acsah. One day Acsah urges Othniel to ask her father for a field, the oldest married move there is: 'Honey, YOU ask him.'

cards.question: When Acsah gets off her donkey, Caleb has a question for her. What does he ask?
Acsah tells Caleb he has given her land in the Negev. What does she ask him to give her as well?
How does Caleb answer his daughter Acsah's request?

answers.text: He gives her the upper and lower springs
He gives her a field beside Hebron
He sends her back to ask Joshua

cards.text: Then comes Judah's inheritance city by city, each with its villages, from the Negev and the foothills to the hill country and the wilderness, with Beersheba, Lachish, Hebron and En-gedi on the list. First time I read it out loud, I lost my place twice and had to start all over at Kabzeel.
Now one last line, and it's about Jerusalem. After that city list, one short verse almost makes me cry happy tears.

cards.question: True or false: The descendants of Judah drive the Jebusites out of Jerusalem.
So how do things stand in Jerusalem "to this day"?

answers.text: The city lies empty and in ruins

findings.problem: The card opens with a fact from outside the passage (Israel is dividing up the land of Canaan, Joshua 14:1) but cites only Joshua 15:1-12, so the outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Joshua and Caleb both appear here for the first time, but the card never says who they are. "Caleb son of Jephunneh" names his father, not who he is, and Joshua gets no description at all.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences ("...does he take a nap?" / "NO." / "He marches against Debir..."). Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This true/false card asks whether the man who captures Kiriath-sepher is Caleb's nephew, but no earlier card says who captures the city or mentions Othniel or Kenaz. The baker can only guess.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The setup for card 15 gives no context to reason from. Saying the verse "almost makes me cry happy tears" also points the baker toward a good outcome (True), when the verse reports that Judah could not drive out the Jebusites.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
